family.name: Inclusive Design Principles

family.r1_licence_field_as_filed: UNPROVEN: no licence statement in fetched text

primary_source.what_it_is_our_words: The principles' own site: seven principles, each with a one-line statement, a full description and examples, in seven languages. The licence is not a sentence on the page — it is a Creative Commons badge in the footer linking to a CC deed.

fetches.size: NOT MEASURED — full page: intro, seven principles with descriptions and examples, footer
fetches.probe_for_licence: footer contains exactly one licence signal: an image whose src is https://i.creativecommons.org/l/by-sa/2.0/uk/88x31.png (the CC BY-SA 2.0 UK badge) wrapped in a link whose href is https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/deed.en (the CC BY-SA 4.0 deed). There is no licence SENTENCE and no copyright line. R1's fetch (curl + tag-stripping) would have dropped both the image and the href, which is why R1 filed UNPROVEN.
fetches.note: Badge version (2.0 UK) and link version (4.0) disagree. Both are Attribution-ShareAlike; the permissions are the same in kind and the attribution/ShareAlike conditions differ only in wording between versions.

fetches.url: WebSearch: "inclusivedesignprinciples.info" github repository license Swan Pouncey Pickering Watson
fetches.outcome: OK — result list only; no repository URL surfaced
fetches.note: Looked for a LICENSE file in a source repository to turn the href into a sentence. Not found by this search; not pursued further.

fetches.http_as_demonstrated: content returned; full legal code, Sections 1-8
fetches.probe_for_licence: Section 2(a)(1) (grant) and Section 3(a)-(b) (Attribution, ShareAlike) read in full. The legal code was fetched rather than the deed the href points to, because the deed is a summary (brief pitfall 1).

licence.name: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike — 4.0 International by the href; 2.0 UK by the badge image
licence.read_from: the licence text itself (CC BY-SA 4.0 legal code, Sections 2 and 3); the APPLICATION of that licence to the site rests on a badge + href, not a sentence
licence.quote_le_15_words: reproduce and Share the Licensed Material, in whole or in part
licence.second_quote_le_15_words: must be a Creative Commons license with the same License Elements, this version or later
licence.second_quote_locus: Section 3(b)(1) — the ShareAlike condition on Adapted Material
licence.grants_our_words: Copy the principles verbatim, in whole or in part, and adapt them — for any purpose, commercial included — provided we credit the creators, link the licence, and mark changes.
licence.forbids_our_words: Sharing an ADAPTATION under any licence other than BY-SA (same elements, this version or later). Verbatim reproduction does not trigger ShareAlike; adaptation that is shared does.

permits_us: reproduce — verbatim node text with attribution; paraphrase — permitted, but a paraphrase is Adapted Material and if it is Shared (emitted into a client deliverable) that adapted text must carry BY-SA
why_our_words: The most generous licence among the thirteen, and R1 had it as UNPROVEN only because a tag-stripping fetch cannot see a badge. The one thing to design for is ShareAlike: a graph node that quotes the principle verbatim with credit is clean; a generator that rewrites it and ships the rewrite into a bank's brief has made Adapted Material and owes BY-SA on that passage. Verbatim-plus-credit is the cheaper posture.
cheap_route_to_lift: Not needed for reproduction. To settle the 2.0-UK-versus-4.0 question and get a sentence instead of a badge: one message to any of the four contributors (links on the page). Price: one message.
unproven: Which BY-SA version the licensor intended — the badge says 2.0 UK, the href says 4.0. This lane treats the href as operative (it is the element a reader follows) and records the disagreement. Price: one contributor message.
Whether the illustrated posters (Barclays Access) are under the same licence — the poster zip was not fetched. Only the page text is tiered here.

pitfalls.what: ShareAlike is contagious to adapted passages: a generator that 'improves' the wording of an inclusive-design node and emits it makes BY-SA text inside a proprietary deliverable. The membership rule should mark this family reproduce-verbatim-preferred.
pitfalls.owner: P2 membership rule author; generator's licence field (a per-family 'adapt?' flag)

pitfalls.what: A badge is not a sentence. If the site ever swaps the footer, the licence signal vanishes with no diff in any text a fetcher stores. Keep the fetch date on the node.
Attribution under 3(a)(1) needs creator names, a licence link and a change indication — three fields, not one string.
